overview: I3201 shifts radio-instrument procedures into FMS/GPS execution. The standard is to load the correct database procedure, understand when GPS is authorized, manage TAA and approach-mode cues, and preserve the missed-approach branch when automatic sequencing stops.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: GPS procedures begin with database and display discipline: the FMS can reduce workload only when the active waypoint, CDI source, and bearing-pointer picture are correct.

children.text: For direct-to navigation, load the desired waypoint, make it active, select FMS as the PFD source, and use the FMS bearing pointer to orient before tracking the CDI.
For GPS intersections, confirm the next waypoint is loaded on the LEGS page before the aircraft reaches the fix.
Approaching a waypoint, the NAV page cue changes from magenta to white over a magenta background, and along-track distance counts down toward 0.0 when crossing directly over the waypoint.
A fly-over waypoint is annotated with /O and must be crossed before turning; after passage, the pointer sequences to the next waypoint.
A fly-by waypoint gives turn anticipation. When the CDI deviation bar flashes, begin a standard-rate turn and intercept or roll out on the new course.
For timing or reporting at a fly-by waypoint, note the time when wings are level and the aircraft is on course or established on an intercept.

items.text: GPS allowable operations are limited by the published procedure, current database, approach title, and whether the underlying NAVAID must still be monitored.

children.text: A published IAP, DP, or STAR must be retrieved by name from a current navigation database; do not manually build an IFR procedure waypoint by waypoint.
Suitable RNAV/GPS may be used to determine position or distance from VOR, VOR/DME, VORTAC, TACAN, NDB, compass locator, DME fixes, and named fixes.
GPS may be used to navigate to or from VOR, TACAN, NDB, compass locator, or DME fixes, and may be used for holding or DME arcs when the rules allow.
Do not use GPS as lateral guidance on a localizer-based final segment unless GPS is in the approach title or the procedure is otherwise specifically authorized.
GPS cannot substitute for the NAVAID providing final approach course guidance, except for procedures titled with GPS or "or GPS" authorization.
If flying the final segment of a VOR, TACAN, or NDB approach with GPS substitution, the underlying NAVAID must be operational and monitored for course alignment.
An alternate airport used for planning must have at least one available non-GPS approach; do not build the alternate plan solely on GPS substitution.
The published chart takes precedence over the GPS display when magnetic variation or database presentation creates a disagreement.

items.text: GPS approaches require correct loading, TAA altitude discipline, approach-mode verification, and a deliberate missed-approach sequence.

children.text: Use LDDHA: load the approach with the correct transition, direct to the IAWP or build the vector-to-final leg as cleared, display FMS, verify any hold or HILO, and confirm APR mode.
A Terminal Arrival Area transitions aircraft from the RNAV en route structure to the terminal area while providing obstacle clearance.
Being cleared direct to an IAF or IF/IAF without an approach clearance does not authorize descent to the lower TAA altitude.
Once cleared for the approach, descend only as authorized by the depicted TAA sector, feeder route, ATC clearance, and published restrictions.
Slow to 150 KIAS within 5 NM of the IAWP when not on radar vectors, then transition to before-approach configuration within 5 NM of the FAWP.
Expect HSI scale-change advisory about 3 NM before the FAWP and verify APR annunciation about 2 NM before the FAWP.
At the FAWP, use the six Ts and descend with about 15 to 20 percent torque, 120 KIAS, and no more than 1000 FPM to LNAV MDA.
The T-6B is certified for RNAV (GPS) approaches to LNAV MDA minimums; do not use VNAV, LNAV/VNAV, or LPV-style vertical minimums.
Level at MDA and continue to the MAWP. If the runway environment is not in sight or landing is unsafe at the MAWP, execute the missed approach.
The FMS will not automatically sequence the missed approach at the MAWP; select MISS APR and execute when the missed approach is required.
If APR mode is not active by 2 NM from the FAWP or GPS integrity is lost before the FAWP, use a backup approach if authorized; otherwise continue at FAWP altitude to the MAWP and go missed.
If GPS integrity is lost inside the FAWP, transition to a backup if authorized, climb to missed-approach altitude, track to the MAWP, execute the missed, and tell ATC as soon as practical.

items.text: GPS holding uses the same holding logic as radio holding, but waypoint passage and abeam cues come from FMS sequencing and along-track distance.

children.text: Confirm the holding waypoint, inbound course, turn direction, leg length or timing, altitude, and EFC before the fix.
When holding at a GPS waypoint, abeam occurs when along-track distance reaches its minimum and begins increasing.
If abeam cannot be determined, start outbound timing when wings are level after the outbound turn.
Use normal holding corrections: track inbound, apply outbound wind correction, and keep speed, altitude, EFC, and fuel in the scan.

items.text: GPS flight modes change CDI sensitivity and required navigation performance, so mode awareness is part of the instrument scan.

children.text: ENR mode uses 2 NM full-scale deflection, or 1 NM per dot.
TERM mode uses 1 NM full-scale deflection, or 0.5 NM per dot.
APR mode uses 0.3 NM full-scale deflection, or 0.15 NM per dot, and displays APR plus the green NPA annunciator.
Departure starts in TERM and normally changes to ENR either more than 33 NM from the origin or above 16,000 feet AGL from origin elevation.
ENR changes to TERM when within 30 NM of the destination and below 15,000 feet AGL from destination elevation.
TERM changes to APR about 2 NM before the FAWP when a valid GPS approach is loaded and integrity is available at the current position, FAWP, and MAP.
APR returns to TERM once MISS APR is selected, with HSI scale returning to 1 NM full scale and RNP returning to 1.0 NM.
At the MAP, the bearing pointer flips and distance-to-go increases, but guidance remains along extended final until MISS APR is manually initiated.

studyNotes.summary: Use the FMS deliberately: load only current database procedures, verify GPS authorization, manage TAA and APR-mode cues, and manually command missed-approach sequencing when required.

summary: GPS procedures, allowable operations, RNAV approach execution, GPS holding, and GPS flight-mode awareness.
title: GPS Procedures
